title: throughput-latency-mismatch-checkin-mar11-2026
body:
Attendees: Marisol (notes), Ethan, Lina, Priya, Jonas

Summary:
- Quick sync to capture the throughput vs latency mismatch we observed after the kernel scheduling change deployed 2026-03-09 (rollout v2.3.7).
- Primary symptom: overall GPU token throughput appears stable for single-sequence long context runs but p95/p99 latency and throughput under mixed-sequence traffic dropped ~18–27% on medium instances (g4x2 equiv).
- Short-term mitigation: revert per-instance kernel affinity for the canary pool (rollback flagged) until we validate KV-cache eviction interaction.

What we saw (notes from bench runs):
- Bench run run://bench-2026-03-10-mixedseq-09 (mixed seq profile: 20% long 80% short) showed: p50 steady, p95 increased from 82ms -> 111ms (+35%), sustained QPS down from 152 -> 119 (-22%).
- Control run single-long-seq run://bench-2026-03-09-long-01 unchanged (p95 stable), indicating the regression surfaces under heterogenous batch composition.
- Kernel rollout PR referenced in linked artifacts appeared to change thread scheduling heuristics; hypothesis: heavier contention on KV cache lifetime leading to more frequent cache misses and suboptimal batching decisions.

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV-cache eviction thrashing: under mixed sequences, longer contexts require large KV slices; eviction policy + new kernel scheduling causes extra copies/locks -> higher tail latency. (High confidence)
2) Batching heuristic mismatch: scheduler now biases slightly larger batches which harms short requests latency; throughput appears lower because short requests wait and cause underfill on some slots. (Medium)
3) NUMA affinity regression on multi-gpu instances causing unexpected memory copy overhead for mixed workloads. (Low/medium)

Data we pulled during meeting:
- Trace snippets: 8 traces captured where p95 spikes align with scattered KV cache refills (trace ids: trace-2026-03-10-07a .. -07h).
- Perf counters: memcpy hotpath spike coincident with GC-like KV eviction events; avg memcpy bytes/sec +28% during spike windows.
- Scheduler logs: batch formation time increased by ~6ms median for mixed-seq runs on canary nodes.

Experiments and quick checks (what we ran / plan to run):
A) Immediate quick rollback (done on canary): repro reduced in canary after rollback; owner: Lina. Status: partial verification.
B) KV-cache eviction policy tweak: extend per-request grace window from 600ms -> 1200ms to reduce churn; run: bench-2026-03-12-kvcache-tweak-01. Owner: Ethan. Status: scheduled.
C) Dedicated mixed-seq microbench (no scheduling change): reproduce baseline on old kernel build to confirm delta. Owner: Priya. Status: running.
D) Batch size floor protection: enforce min batch delay of 2ms for short seqs to avoid starvation under new scheduler. Owner: Jonas. Status: prototype coded (branch: perf/min-batch-delay).
E) NUMA memory pinning validation: collect multi-GPU copy stats across instance types. Owner: Marisol. Status: scheduled.

Preliminary results (first 24h):
- Rollback on canary reduced p95 by ~20% for mixed runs but did not restore QPS fully to baseline. This suggests multiple contributors.
- The KV-cache grace window patch in a small run reduced memcpy peaks but increased memory footprint; estimate +4.5% memory pressure on medium nodes.

Action items (owners & deadlines):
- Ethan: run extended KV-cache-tweak matrix (grace window 800ms/1200ms/1600ms) across three instance sizes, capture p50/p95/p99 and memory usage. Due 2026-03-14.
- Lina: coordinate canary rollback telemetry check and postmortem stub in INF-2543. Due 2026-03-13.
- Priya: complete baseline microbench on old kernel and upload traces to bench artifact. Due 2026-03-13.
- Jonas: land min-batch-delay prototype to perf branch and run AB tests with small traffic to measure short-request latency. Due 2026-03-15.
- Marisol: collect NUMA/copy counters and add to the shared perf dashboard widget. Due 2026-03-16.

Open questions / discussion points for next sync:
- Is there appetite to prioritize KV-cache memory optimization vs scheduler revert? Memory-sensitive customers could prefer scheduler rollback; cost-sensitive customers prefer code-level fix.
- If grace-window increases memory by >6% at 99th percentile, what's the threshold for reverting? Need cost estimates from infra.
- Can we instrument batch-formation per-request tagging earlier in pipeline to quickly attribute latency to batching vs copy? (instrumentation effort ~1.5d)

Notes to self (raw):
- Check whether PR 1012 included any implicit lock order changes — grep for mutex reorders.
- Add synthetic workload that flips short/long ratio every 30s to stress KV churn.

Meeting cadence / next touchpoints:
- Quick async updates in #perf-bench by EOD daily until stable.
- Follow-up sync Thu 2026-03-13 10:00 PT; agenda: finalizing experiment matrix, cost tradeoffs, rollback decision window.

Appendix (run references & short commands):
- reproduce locally (mixed): ./bench/run_mixed.sh --profile mixedseq --nodes canary --runs 50 --traceout traces/mixed-$(date +%F)-run
- decode trace: tools/trace_inspect --id trace-2026-03-10-07c --span kv-evict
- bench artifacts: run://bench-2026-03-10-mixedseq-09, run://bench-2026-03-09-long-01, run://bench-2026-03-12-kvcache-tweak-01

Owners pinged for reviews: @efpark, @lzhou, @pnair, @jkeller

-- end notes
